lines.hook: What if you built a ladder all the way to space, and climbed it?
lines.goal: Space starts sixty-two miles up. Let's see if he makes it.
lines.tower: Twenty-seven hundred feet. He just passed the tallest building on Earth.
lines.halfair: Eighteen thousand feet. Half of all the air on Earth is now below him.
lines.everest: Twenty-nine thousand feet. Higher than Everest. Without his suit, he'd pass out in about a minute.
lines.plane: Thirty-seven thousand feet. Planes fly here, and so did the highest flying bird ever recorded.
lines.armstrong: Sixty-two thousand feet. Up here, without a suit, his spit would literally boil.
lines.skydive: Twenty-five miles. The highest anyone has ever skydived from. And he's not even halfway.
lines.meteors: Fifty-three miles. The coldest air on the planet, minus a hundred and thirty degrees. Shooting stars burn up all around him.
lines.space: And he made it. Sixty-two miles. Space.
lines.tail: But if he lets go, he falls straight back down. To stay up here, you'd have to fly seventeen thousand miles an hour, sideways.
lines.outro: Space is close. Staying there is the hard part.
